title: Food service sanitation rules: the practical minimum
excerpt: A small café needs roughly ten logs and three or four procedures as its basic minimum. Six items address 80% of inspection findings; the rest is paperwork inherited from another era.

body.text: Sanitation rules for food service run to hundreds of pages. Reading them all can be discouraging. In practice, the mandatory minimum for a small establishment fits into about ten logs and three or four regular procedures.

items: Raw-material receipt and incoming inspection log.
Production control programme and DDD log (disinfection, disinsection and deratization).

body.title: Why these items
body.text: These six items cover 80% of inspectors' findings and 100% of situations involving an investigation of food poisoning.

Separate certificates, paper plans, and duplicate entries of the same data in different logs are all remnants of an era without a unified system. With electronic recordkeeping, one entry (for example, a goods receipt) can feed several logs, so nothing needs to be copied by hand.
